items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: it was the first time I was in Europe with Slam Stewart trio, with Earl Garner, myself and Slam.

ctx.x: arrangement during rehearsal in B flat, and so we're going to do this tune tonight, we're going to get to work. And Beryl is juiced and she'd get to where we did it, she'd play the whole thing in B natural, which is the hardest key in the world, and play it note for note, nothing -- you know, nothing changed.

And I would say Beryl, come on, B flat. She said, man, I thought it was B natural. She was a tremendous piano player. But any way she got ill and then Earl came with us, Earl Grant -- Earl Garner, what am I saying Grant, Earl Garner. As a matter of fact we went to Europe together, it was the first time I was in Europe with Slam Stewart trio, with Earl Garner, myself and Slam. And --
